entries.ef017328176929702ca6f7835d4d5d5d9b6ae68d: <div sID="gen34290" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="22" osisID="Rev.22" sID="Rev.22"/> <div eID="gen34290" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34291" type="x-p"/> In this chapter we have, I. A further description of the heavenly state of the church, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.1-Rev.22.5">ver. 1-5</reference>. II. A confirmation of this and all the other visions of this book, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.6-Rev.22.19">ver. 6-19</reference>. III. The conclusion, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.20-Rev.22.21">ver. 20, 21</reference>.
entries.2117fa662635acfaec522b6e42950bb8ddda6e9b: <div eID="gen34291" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The New Jerusalem. (<hi type="small-caps">a. d.</hi> 95.)</title> <div sID="gen34292" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> And he showed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb. <hi type="super">2</hi> In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, <hi type="italic">was there</hi> the tree of life, which bare twelve <hi type="italic">manner of</hi> fruits, <hi type="italic">and</hi> yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree <hi type="italic">were</hi> for the healing of the nations. <hi type="super">3</hi> And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him: <hi type="super">4</hi> And they shall see his face; and his name <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> in their foreheads. <hi type="super">5</hi> And there shall be no night there; and they need no candle, neither light of the sun; for the Lord God giveth them light: and they shall reign for ever and ever. <div eID="gen34292" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34293" type="x-p"/> The heavenly state which was before described as a city, and called the new Jerusalem, is here described as a paradise, alluding to the earthly paradise which was lost by the sin of the first Adam; here is another paradise restored by the second Adam. A paradise in a city, or a whole city in a paradise! In the first paradise there were only two persons to behold the beauty and taste the pleasures of it; but in this second paradise whole cities and nations shall find abundant delight and satisfaction. And here observe, <div eID="gen34293" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34294" type="x-p"/> I. The river of paradise. The earthly paradise was well watered: no place can be pleasant or fruitful that is not so. This river is described, 1. By its fountain-head—<hi type="italic">the throne of God and the Lamb.</hi> All our springs of grace, comfort, and glory, are in God; and all our streams from him are through the mediation of the Lamb. 2. By its quality—<hi type="italic">pure and clear as crystal.</hi> All the streams of earthly comfort are muddy; but these are clear, salutary, and refreshing, giving life, and preserving life, to those who drink of them. <div eID="gen34294" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34295" type="x-p"/> II. The tree of life, in this paradise. Such a tree there was in the earthly paradise, <reference osisRef="Gen.2.9">Gen. ii. 9</reference>. This far excels it. And now, as to this tree, observe, 1. The situation of it—<hi type="italic">in the midst of the street, and on either side the river;</hi> or, as might have been better rendered, <hi type="italic">in the midst between the terrace-walk and the river.</hi> This tree of life is fed by the pure waters of the river that comes from the throne of God. The presence and perfections of God furnish out all the glory and blessedness of heaven. 2. The fruitfulness of this tree. (1.) It brings forth many sorts of fruit—<hi type="italic">twelve sorts,</hi> suited to the refined taste of all the saints. (2.) It brings forth fruit at all times—<hi type="italic">yields its fruit every month.</hi> This tree is never empty, never barren; there is always fruit upon it. In heaven there is not only a variety of pure and satisfying pleasures, but a continuance of them, and always fresh. (3.) The fruit is not only pleasant, but wholesome. The presence of God in heaven is the health and happiness of the saints; there they find in him a remedy for all their former maladies, and are preserved by him in the most healthful and vigorous state. <div eID="gen34295" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34296" type="x-p"/> III. The perfect freedom of this paradise from every thing that is evil (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.3">v. 3</reference>): <hi type="italic">There shall be no more curse;</hi> no <hi type="italic">accursed one</hi>—<hi type="bold"><hi type="italic">katanathema,</hi></hi> no serpent there, as there was in the earthly paradise. Here is the great excellency of this paradise. The devil has nothing to do there; he cannot draw the saints from serving God to be subject to himself, as he did our first parents, nor can he so much as disturb them in the service of God. <div eID="gen34296" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34297" type="x-p"/> IV. The supreme felicity of this paradisiacal state. 1. There the saints shall see the face of God; there they shall enjoy the beatific vision. 2. God will own them, as having his seal and name on their foreheads. 3. <hi type="italic">They shall reign with him for ever;</hi> their service shall be not only freedom but honour and dominion. 4. All this shall be with perfect knowledge and joy. They shall be full of wisdom and comfort, continually walking in the light of the Lord; and this not for a time, <hi type="italic">but for ever and ever.</hi>
entries.38a761df4820fdc2dc95896fcb739dbc5769f935: <div eID="gen34297" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The New Jerusalem. (<hi type="small-caps">a. d.</hi> 95.)</title> <div sID="gen34298" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">6</hi> And he said unto me, These sayings <hi type="italic">are</hi> faithful and true: and the Lord God of the holy prophets sent his angel to show unto his servants the things which must shortly be done. <hi type="super">7</hi> Behold, I come quickly: blessed <hi type="italic">is</hi> he that keepeth the sayings of the prophecy of this book. <hi type="super">8</hi> And I John saw these things, and heard <hi type="italic">them.</hi> And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which showed me these things. <hi type="super">9</hi> Then saith he unto me, See <hi type="italic">thou do it</hi> not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God. <hi type="super">10</hi> And he saith unto me, Seal not the sayings of the prophecy of this book: for the time is at hand. <hi type="super">11</hi> He that is unjust, let him be unjust still: and he which is filthy, let him be filthy still: and he that is righteous, let him be righteous still: and he that is holy, let him be holy still. <hi type="super">12</hi> And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward <hi type="italic">is</hi> with me, to give every man according as his work shall be. <hi type="super">13</hi> I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last. <hi type="super">14</hi> Blessed <hi type="italic">are</hi> they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city. <hi type="super">15</hi> For without <hi type="italic">are</hi> dogs, and sorcerers, and whoremongers, and murderers, and idolaters, and whosoever loveth and maketh a lie. <hi type="super">16</hi> I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the bright and morning star. <hi type="super">17</hi> And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely. <hi type="super">18</hi> For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book: <hi type="super">19</hi> And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city, and <hi type="italic">from</hi> the things which are written in this book. <div eID="gen34298" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34299" type="x-p"/> We have here a solemn ratification of the contents of this book, and particularly of this last vision (though some think it may not only refer to the whole book, but to the whole New Testament, yea, to the whole Bible, completing and confirming the can on of scripture); and here, 1. This is confirmed by the name and nature of that God who gave out these discoveries: he is <hi type="italic">the Lord God, faithful and true,</hi> and so are all his sayings. 2. By the messengers he chose, to reveal these things to the world; the holy angels showed them to holy men of God; and God would not employ his saints and angels in deceiving the world. 3. They will soon be confirmed by their accomplishment: they are things that must shortly be done; Christ will make haste, <hi type="italic">he will come quickly,</hi> and put all things out of doubt; and then those will prove the wise and happy men who have believed and kept his words. 4. By the integrity of that angel who had been the apostle's guide and interpreter in these visions; this integrity was such that he not only refused to accept religious adoration from John, but once and again reproved him for it. He who was so tender of the honour of God, and so displeased with what was a wrong to God, would never come in his name to lead the people of God into mere dreams and delusions; and it is a still further confirmation of the sincerity of this apostle that he confesses his own sin and folly, into which he had now again relapsed, and he leaves this his failing on perpetual record: this shows he was a faithful and an impartial writer. 5. By the order given to leave the book of the prophecy open, to be perused by all, that they might labour to understand it, that they might make their objections against it, and compare the prophecy with the events. God here deals freely and openly with all; he does not speak in secret, but calls every one to witness to the declarations here made, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.10">v. 10</reference>. 6. By the effect this book, thus kept open, will have upon men; those that are filthy and unjust will take occasion thence to be more so, but it will confirm, strengthen, and further sanctify those that are upright with God; it will be a savour of life to some and of death to others, and so will appear to be from God, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.12">v. 12</reference>. 7. It will be Christ's rule of judgment at the great day; he will dispense rewards and punishments to men according as their works agree or disagree with the word of God; and therefore that word itself must needs be faithful and true. 8. It is the word of him who is the author, finisher, and rewarder of the faith and holiness of his people, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.13-Rev.22.14">v. 13, 14</reference>. He is <hi type="italic">the first and the last,</hi> and the same from first to last, and so is his word too; and he will by this word give to his people, who conform themselves to it, <hi type="italic">a right to the tree of life,</hi> and an entrance into heaven; and this will be a full confirmation of the truth and authority of his word, since it contains the title and evidence of that confirmed state of holiness and happiness that remains for his people in heaven. 9. It is a book that condemns and excludes from heaven all wicked, unrighteous persons, and particularly <hi type="italic">those that love and make lies</hi> (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.15">v. 15</reference>), and therefore can never be itself a lie. 10. It is confirmed by <hi type="italic">the testimony of Jesus, which is the Spirit of prophecy.</hi> And this Jesus, as God, is <hi type="italic">the root of David,</hi> though, as man, his offspring—a person in whom all uncreated and created excellencies meet, too great and too good to deceive his churches and the world. He is the fountain of all light, the <hi type="italic">bright and the morning star,</hi> and as such has given to his churches this morning light of prophecy, to assure them of the light of that perfect day which is approaching. 11. It is confirmed by an open and general invitation to all to come and partake of the promises and privileges of the gospel, those streams of the water of life; these are tendered to all who feel in their souls a thirst which nothing in this world can quench. 12. It is confirmed by the joint testimony of the Spirit of God, and that gracious Spirit that is in all the true members of the church of God; <hi type="italic">the Spirit and the bride</hi> join in testifying the truth and excellency of the gospel. 13. It is confirmed by a most solemn sanction, condemning and cursing all who should dare to corrupt or change the word of God, either by adding to it or taking from it, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.18-Rev.22.19">v. 18, 19</reference>. He that adds to the word of God draws down upon himself <hi type="italic">all the plagues written in this book;</hi> and he who takes any thing away from it cuts himself off from all the promises and privileges of it. This sanction is like a flaming sword, to guard the canon of the scripture from profane hands. Such a fence as this God set about the law (<reference osisRef="Deut.4.2">Deut. iv. 2</reference>), and the whole Old Testament (<reference osisRef="Mal.4.4">Mal. iv. 4</reference>), and now in the most solemn manner about the whole Bible, assuring us that it is a book of the most sacred nature, divine authority, and of the last importance, and therefore the peculiar care of the great God.
entries.74b732d50eb60675c11ae40986da9a4a2ec809ab: <div eID="gen34299" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">Conclusion. (<hi type="small-caps">a. d.</hi> 95.)</title> <div sID="gen34300" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">20</hi> He which testifieth these things saith, Surely I come quickly. Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus. <hi type="super">21</hi> The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ <hi type="italic">be</hi> with you all. Amen. <div eID="gen34300" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34301" type="x-p"/> We have now come to the conclusion of the whole, and that in three things:— <div eID="gen34301" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34302" type="x-p"/> I. Christ's farewell to his church. He seems now, after he has been discovering these things to his people on earth, to take leave of them, and return to heaven; but he parts with them in great kindness, and assures them it shall not be long before he comes again to them: <hi type="italic">Behold, I come quickly.</hi> As when he ascended into heaven, after his resurrection, he parted with a promise of his gracious presence, so here he parts with a promise of a speedy return. If any say, "Where is the promise of his coming, when so many ages have passed since this was written?" let them know he is not slack to his people, but long-suffering to his enemies: his coming will be sooner than they are aware, sooner than they are prepared, sooner than they desire; and to his people it will be seasonable. The vision is for an appointed time, and will not tarry. <hi type="italic">He will come quickly;</hi> let this word be always sounding in our ear, and let us give all diligence that we may be found of him in peace, <hi type="italic">without spot and blameless.</hi> <div eID="gen34302" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34303" type="x-p"/> II. The church's hearty echo to Christ's promise, 1. Declaring her firm belief of it: <hi type="italic">Amen, so it is,</hi> so it shall be. 2. Expressing her earnest desire of it: <hi type="italic">Even so, come, Lord Jesus; make hast, my beloved, and be thou like a roe, or like a young hart on the mountain of spices.</hi> Thus beats the pulse of the church, thus breathes that gracious Spirit which actuates and informs the mystical body of Christ; and we should never be satisfied till we find such a spirit breathing in us, and causing us to <hi type="italic">look for the blessed hope, and glorious appearance of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ.</hi> This is the language of the church of the first-born, and we should join with them, often putting ourselves in mind of his promise. What comes from heaven in a promise should be sent back to heaven in a prayer, "<hi type="italic">Come, Lord Jesus,</hi> put an end to this state of sin, sorrow, and temptation; gather thy people out of this present evil world, and take them up to heaven, that state of perfect purity, peace, and joy, and so finish thy great design, and fulfil all that word in which thou hast caused thy people to hope." <div eID="gen34303" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34304" type="x-p"/> III. The apostolical benediction, which closes the whole: <hi type="italic">The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all, Amen.</hi> Here observe, 1. The Bible ends with a clear proof of the Godhead of Christ, since the Spirit of God teaches the apostle to bless his people in the name of Christ, and to beg from Christ a blessing for them, which is a proper act of adoration. 2. Nothing should be more desired by us than that the grace of Christ may be with us in this world, to prepare us for the glory of Christ in the other world. It is by his grace that we must be kept in a joyful expectation of his glory, fitted for it, and preserved to it; and his glorious appearance will be welcome and joyful to those that are partakers of his grace and favour here; and therefore to this most comprehensive prayer we should all add our hearty <hi type="italic">Amen,</hi> most earnestly thirsting after greater measures of the gracious influences of the blessed Jesus in our souls, and his gracious presence with us, till glory has perfected all his grace towards us, for he is a sun and a shield, <hi type="italic">he gives grace and glory, and no good thing will he withhold from those that walk uprightly.</hi> <<< <chapter eID="Rev.22"/> <div eID="gen34304" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen33890" osisID="Rev" type="book"/>

entries.340fa773182de52790f7c2305c516fdaae68042b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19420"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 22</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Rev.22.1-Rev.22.21">Re 22:1-21</reference>. The River of Life: The Tree of Life: The Other Blessednesses of the Redeemed. John Forbidden to Worship the Angel. Nearness of Christ's Coming to Fix Man's Eternal State. Testimony of Jesus, His Spirit, and the Bride, Any Addition to Which, or Subtraction from Which, Shall Be Eternally Punished. Closing Benediction.</title> <div sID="gen42541" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19420"/><hi type="bold">1. pure--</hi>A, B, Vulgate, and Hilary 22, omit.<div eID="gen42541" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42542" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">water of life--</hi>infinitely superior to the typical waters in the first Paradise (<reference osisRef="Gen.2.10-Gen.2.14">Ge 2:10-14</reference>); and even superior to those figurative ones in the millennial Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="Ezek.47.1">Eze 47:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.47.12">12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.8">Zec 14:8</reference>), as the matured fruit is superior to the flower. The millennial waters represent full Gospel grace; these waters of new Jerusalem represent Gospel glory perfected. Their continuous flow from God, the Fountain of life, symbolizes the uninterrupted continuance of life derived by the saints, ever fresh, from Him: life in fulness of joy, as well as perpetual vitality. Like pure crystal, it is free from every taint: compare <reference osisRef="Rev.4.6">Re 4:6</reference>, "before the throne a sea of glass, like crystal."<div eID="gen42542" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42543" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">clear--</hi>Greek, "bright." <div eID="gen42543" type="x-p"/>
entries.6bf9a36986875716e991eacfbbc8f72b8504050a: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19421"/><div sID="gen42544" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19421"/>2. The harmonious unity of Scripture is herein exhibited. The Fathers compared it to a ring, an unbroken circle, returning into itself. Between the events of Genesis and those at the close of the Apocalypse, at least six thousand or seven thousand years intervene; and between Moses the first writer and John the last about one thousand five hundred years. How striking it is that, as in the beginning we found Adam and Eve, his bride, in innocence m Paradise, then tempted by the serpent, and driven from the tree of life, and from the pleasant waters of Eden, yet not without a promise of a Redeemer who should crush the serpent; so at the close, the old serpent cast out for ever by the second Adam, the Lord from heaven, who appears with His Bride, the Church, in a better Paradise, and amidst better waters (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.1">Re 22:1</reference>): the tree of life also is there with all its healing properties, not guarded with a flaming sword, but open to all who overcome (<reference osisRef="Rev.2.7">Re 2:7</reference>), and there is no more curse.<div eID="gen42544" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42545" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">street of it--</hi>that is, of the city.<div eID="gen42545" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42546" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">on either side of the river--</hi>Alford translates, "In the midst of the street of it (the city) and of the river, on one side and on the other" (for the second Greek, "enteuthen," A, B, and Syriac read, ekeithen: the sense is the same; compare Greek, <reference osisRef="John.19.18">Joh 19:18</reference>); thus the trees were on each side in the middle of the space between the street and the river. But from <reference osisRef="Ezek.47.7">Eze 47:7</reference>, I prefer English Version. The antitype exceeds the type: in the first Paradise was only one tree of life; now there are "very many trees at the bank of the river, on the one side and on the other." To make good sense, supposing there to be but one tree, we should either, as Mede, suppose that the Greek for street is a plain washed on both sides by the river (as the first Paradise was washed on one side by the Tigris, on the other by the Euphrates), and that in the midst of the plain, which itself is in the midst of the river's branches, stood the tree: in which case we may translate, "In the midst of the street (plain) itself, and of the river (having two branches flowing) on this and on that side, was there the tree of life." Or else with Durham suppose, the tree was in the midst of the river, and extending its branches to both banks. But compare <reference osisRef="Ezek.47.12">Eze 47:12</reference>, the millennial type of the final Paradise; which shows that there are several trees of the one kind, all termed "the tree of life." Death reigns now because of sin; even in the millennial earth sin, and therefore death, though much limited, shall not altogether cease. But in the final and heavenly city on earth, sin and death shall utterly cease.<div eID="gen42546" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42547" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">yielded her fruit every month--</hi>Greek, "according to each month"; each month had its own proper fruit, just as different seasons are now marked by their own productions; only that then, unlike now, there shall be no season without its fruit, and there shall be an endless variety, answering to twelve, the number symbolical of the world-wide Church (compare Note, see on <reference osisRef="Rev.12.1">Re 12:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.21.14">Re 21:14</reference>). Archbishop Whatley thinks that the tree of life was among the trees of which Adam freely ate (<reference osisRef="Gen.2.9">Ge 2:9</reference>, 16, 17), and that his continuance in immortality was dependent on his continuing to eat of this tree; having forfeited it, he became liable to death; but still the effects of having eaten of it for a time showed themselves in the longevity of the patriarchs. God could undoubtedly endue a tree with special medicinal powers. But <reference osisRef="Gen.3.22">Ge 3:22</reference> seems to imply, man had not yet taken of the tree, and that if he had, he would have lived for ever, which in his then fallen state would have been the greatest curse.<div eID="gen42547" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42548" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">leaves ... for ... healing--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ezek.47.9">Eze 47:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.47.12">12</reference>). The leaves shall be the health-giving preventive securing the redeemed against, not healing them of, sicknesses, while "the fruit shall be for meat." In the millennium described in <reference osisRef="Ezek.47.1-Ezek.47.23">Eze 47:1-23</reference> and <reference osisRef="Rev.20.1-Rev.20.15">Re 20:1-15</reference>, the Church shall give the Gospel-tree to the nations outside Israel and the Church, and so shall heal their spiritual malady; but in the final and perfect new Jerusalem here described, the state of all is eternally fixed, and no saving process goes on any longer (compare <reference osisRef="Rev.22.11">Re 22:11</reference>). Alford utterly mistakes in speaking of "nations outside," and "dwelling on the renewed earth, organized under kings, and saved by the influences of the heavenly city" (!) Compare <reference osisRef="Rev.21.2">Re 21:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.21.10-Rev.21.27">10-27</reference>; the "nations" mentioned (<reference osisRef="Rev.21.24">Re 21:24</reference>) are those which have long before, namely, in the millennium (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.15">Re 11:15</reference>), become the Lord's and His Christ's. <div eID="gen42548" type="x-p"/>
entries.ed2e92bae47fc5b96121c576cd796476d28b661f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19422"/><div sID="gen42549" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19422"/><hi type="bold">3. no more curse--</hi>of which the earnest shall be given in the millennium (<reference osisRef="Zech.14.11">Zec 14:11</reference>). God can only dwell where the curse and its cause, the cursed thing sin (<reference osisRef="Josh.7.12">Jos 7:12</reference>), are removed. So there follows rightly, "But the throne of God and of the Lamb (who redeemed us from the curse, <reference osisRef="Gal.3.10">Ga 3:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gal.3.13">13</reference>) shall be in it." Compare in the millennium, <reference osisRef="Ezek.48.35">Eze 48:35</reference>.<div eID="gen42549" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42550" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">serve him--</hi>with worship (<reference osisRef="Rev.7.15">Re 7:15</reference>). <div eID="gen42550" type="x-p"/>
entries.7fabade83972921e6302dea869c5d8cea550a7a1: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19423"/><div sID="gen42551" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19423"/><hi type="bold">4. see his face--</hi>revealed in divine glory, in Christ Jesus. They shall see and know Him with intuitive knowledge of Him, even as they are known by Him (<reference osisRef="1Cor.13.9-1Cor.13.12">1Co 13:9-12</reference>), and face to face. Compare <reference osisRef="1Tim.6.16">1Ti 6:16</reference>, with <reference osisRef="John.14.9">Joh 14:9</reference>. God the Father can only be seen in Christ.<div eID="gen42551" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42552" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in--</hi>Greek, "on their foreheads." Not only shall they personally and in secret (<reference osisRef="Rev.3.17">Re 3:17</reference>) know their sonship, but they shall be known as sons of God to all the citizens of the new Jerusalem, so that the free flow of mutual love among the members of Christ's family will not be checked by suspicion as here. <div eID="gen42552" type="x-p"/>
entries.014b56a67769e5232c110064224cac8b90e333a5: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19424"/><div sID="gen42553" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19424"/><hi type="bold">5. there--</hi>so Andreas. But A, B, Vulgate, and Syriac read, "(there shall be no night) any longer"; Greek, "eti," for "ekei."<div eID="gen42553" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42554" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">they need--</hi>A, Vulgate, and Coptic read the future, "they shall not have need." B reads, "(and there shall be) no need."<div eID="gen42554" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42555" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">candle--</hi>Greek, "lamp." A, Vulgate, Syriac, and Coptic insert "light (of a candle, or lamp)." B Omits it.<div eID="gen42555" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42556" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">of the sun--</hi>so A. But B omits it.<div eID="gen42556" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42557" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">giveth ... light--</hi>"illumines." So Vulgate and Syriac. But A reads, "shall give light."<div eID="gen42557" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42558" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">them--</hi>so B and Andreas. But A reads, "upon them."<div eID="gen42558" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42559" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">reign--</hi>with a glory probably transcending that of their reign in heaven with Christ over the millennial nations in the flesh described in <reference osisRef="Rev.20.4">Re 20:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.20.6">6</reference>; that reign was but for a limited time, "a thousand years"; this final reign is "unto the ages of the ages." <div eID="gen42559" type="x-p"/>
entries.b6fa846d4ef9e5e0332021f36fa85a3c62f45e77: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19425"/><div sID="gen42560" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19425"/><hi type="bold">6. These sayings are true--</hi>thrice repeated (<reference osisRef="Rev.19.9">Re 19:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.21.5">21:5</reference>). For we are slow to believe that God is as good as He is. The news seems to us, habituated as we are to the misery of this fallen world, too good to be true [Nangle]. They are no dreams of a visionary, but the realities of God's sure word.<div eID="gen42560" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42561" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">holy--</hi>so Andreas. But A, B, Vulgate, Syriac, and Coptic read, "(the Lord God of the) spirits (of the prophets)." The Lord God who with His Spirit inspired their spirits so as to be able to prophesy. There is but one Spirit, but individual prophets, according to the measure given them (<reference osisRef="1Cor.12.4-1Cor.12.11">1Co 12:4-11</reference>), had their own spirits [Bengel] (<reference osisRef="1Pet.1.11">1Pe 1:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Pet.1.21">2Pe 1:21</reference>).<div eID="gen42561" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42562" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">be done--</hi>Greek, "come to pass." <div eID="gen42562" type="x-p"/>
entries.282af0bd47d8ec36a2780c88feadef63e2fd519d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19426"/><div sID="gen42563" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19426"/>7. "And" is omitted in Coptic and Andreas with English Version, but is inserted by A, B, Vulgate and Syriac.<div eID="gen42563" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42564" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">blessed--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Rev.1.3">Re 1:3</reference>). <div eID="gen42564" type="x-p"/>
entries.ebf57d8e826ec017b5abdc968c771ba26e739d80: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19427"/><div sID="gen42565" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19427"/>8. Both here and in <reference osisRef="Rev.19.9">Re 19:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.19.10">10</reference>, the apostle's falling at the feet of the angel is preceded by a glorious promise to the Church, accompanied with the assurance, that "These are the true sayings of God," and that those are "blessed" who keep them. Rapturous emotion, gratitude, and adoration, at the prospect of the Church's future glory transport him out of himself, so as all but to fall into an unjustifiable act; contrast his opposite feeling at the prospect of the Church's deep fall [Auberlen], see on <reference osisRef="Rev.17.6">Re 17:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.19.9">Re 19:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.19.10">10</reference>.<div eID="gen42565" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42566" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">saw ... and heard--</hi>A, B, Vulgate, and Syriac transpose these verbs. Translate literally, "I John (was he) who heard and saw these things." It is observable that in <reference osisRef="Rev.19.10">Re 19:10</reference>, the language is, "I fell before his feet to worship him"; but here, "I fell down to worship (God?) before the feet of the angel." It seems unlikely that John, when once reproved, would fall into the very same error again. Bengel's view, therefore, is probable; John had first intended to worship the angel (<reference osisRef="Rev.19.10">Re 19:10</reference>), but now only at his feet intends to worship (God). The angel does not even permit this. <div eID="gen42566" type="x-p"/>
entries.3baa59a9ddcbcd11710f99452d8f4240bae8bd2c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19428"/><div sID="gen42567" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19428"/>9. Literally, "See not"; the abruptness of the phrase marking the angel's abhorrence of the thought of his being worshipped however indirectly. Contrast the fallen angel's temptation to Jesus, "Fall down and worship me" (<reference osisRef="Matt.4.9">Mt 4:9</reference>).<div eID="gen42567" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42568" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">for--</hi>A, B, Vulgate, Syriac, Coptic, Andreas, and Cyprian omit "for"; which accords with the abrupt earnestness of the angel's prohibition of an act derogatory to God.<div eID="gen42568" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42569" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and of--</hi>"and (the fellow servant) of thy brethren." <div eID="gen42569" type="x-p"/>
entries.afaf9773babdf27a1abba7464069d3667d526d1f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19429"/><div sID="gen42570" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19429"/><hi type="bold">10. Seal not--</hi>But in <reference osisRef="Dan.12.4">Da 12:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Dan.12.9">9</reference> (compare <reference osisRef="Dan.8.26">Da 8:26</reference>), the command is, "Seal the book," for the vision shall be "for many days." The fulfilment of Daniel's prophecy was distant, that of John's prophecy is near. The New Testament is the time of the end and fulfilment. The Gentile Church, for which John wrote his Revelation, needs more to be impressed with the shortness of the period, as it is inclined, owing to its Gentile origin, to conform to the world and forget the coming of the Lord. The Revelation points, on the one hand, to Christ's coming as distant, for it shows the succession of the seven seals, trumpets, and vials; on the other hand, it proclaims, "Behold, I come quickly." So Christ marked many events as about to intervene before His coming, and yet He also says "Behold, I come quickly," because our right attitude is that of continual prayerful watching for His coming (<reference osisRef="Matt.25.6">Mt 25:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.13.19">13, 19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mark.13.32-Mark.13.37">Mr 13:32-37</reference> [Auberlen]; compare <reference osisRef="Rev.1.3">Re 1:3</reference>). <div eID="gen42570" type="x-p"/>
entries.89aa22f2f6877578588bbbae6c90422c647f9291: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19430"/><div sID="gen42571" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19430"/><hi type="bold">11. unjust--</hi>"unrighteous"; in relation to one's fellow men; opposed to "righteous," or "just" (as the Greek may be translated) below. More literally, "he that doeth unjustly, let him do unjustly still."<div eID="gen42571" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42572" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">filthy--</hi>in relation to one's own soul as unclean before God; opposed to holy," consecrated to God as pure. A omits the clause, "He which is filthy let him be filthy still." But B supports it. In the letter of the Vienne and Lyons Martyrs (in Eusebius) in the second century, the reading is, "He that is lawless (Greek, 'anomos') let him be lawless; and he that is righteous let him be righteous (literally, 'be justified') still." No manuscript is so old. A, B, Vulgate, Syriac, Coptic, Andreas, and Cyprian read, "let him do righteousness" (<reference osisRef="1John.2.29">1Jo 2:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.3.7">3:7</reference>). The punishment of sin is sin, the reward of holiness is holiness. Eternal punishment is not so much an arbitrary law, as a result necessarily following in the very nature of things, as the fruit results from the bud. No worse punishment can God lay on ungodly men than to give them up to themselves. The solemn lesson derivable from this verse is, Be converted now in the short time left (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.10">Re 22:10</reference>, end) before "I come" (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.7">Re 22:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.12">12</reference>), or else you must remain unconverted for ever; sin in the eternal world will be left to its own natural consequences; holiness in germ will there develop itself into perfect holiness, which is happiness. <div eID="gen42572" type="x-p"/>
entries.e4cfbf5efb8e78d22f2cdb3e52b40b53ce20018c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19431"/><div sID="gen42573" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19431"/><hi type="bold">12. And--</hi>in none of our manuscripts. But A, B, Vulgate, Syriac, Coptic, and Cyprian omit it.<div eID="gen42573" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42574" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">behold, I come quickly--</hi>(Compare <reference osisRef="Rev.22.7">Re 22:7</reference>).<div eID="gen42574" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42575" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">my reward is with me--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.40.10">Is 40:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.62.11">62:11</reference>).<div eID="gen42575" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42576" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to give--</hi>Greek, "to render."<div eID="gen42576" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42577" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">every man--</hi>Greek, "to each."<div eID="gen42577" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42578" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall be--</hi>so B in Mai. But B in Tischendorf, and A, Syriac, read, "is." <div eID="gen42578" type="x-p"/>
entries.9e29daaf410d18734cf9657869889558c19b4ccf: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19432"/><div sID="gen42579" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19432"/><hi type="bold">13. I am Alpha--</hi>Greek, "... the Alpha and the Omega." A, B, Vulgate, Syriac, Origen, and Cyprian transpose thus, "the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End." Andreas supports English Version. Compare with these divine titles assumed here by the Lord Jesus, <reference osisRef="Rev.1.8">Re 1:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.17">17</reference>; 21:6. At the winding up of the whole scheme of revelation He announces Himself as the One before whom and after whom there is no God. <div eID="gen42579" type="x-p"/>
entries.dd110be49158004e8a69fac200667278316834e5: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19433"/><div sID="gen42580" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19433"/><hi type="bold">14. do his commandments--</hi>so B, Syriac, Coptic, and Cyprian. But A, Aleph, and Vulgate read, "(Blessed are they that) wash their robes," namely, in the blood of the Lamb (compare <reference osisRef="Rev.7.14">Re 7:14</reference>). This reading takes away the pretext for the notion of salvation by works. But even English Version reading is quite compatible with salvation by grace; for God's first and grand Gospel "commandment" is to believe on Jesus. Thus our "right" to (Greek, "privilege" or "lawful authority over") the tree of life is due not to our doings, but to what He has done for us. The right, or privilege, is founded, not on our merits, but on God's grace.<div eID="gen42580" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42581" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">through--</hi>Greek, "by the gates." <div eID="gen42581" type="x-p"/>
entries.6390e38e21382596c8ade01621f697dff6a846c9: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19434"/><div sID="gen42582" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19434"/><hi type="bold">15. But--</hi>so Coptic. But A, B, Hippolytus, Andreas, and Cyprian omit.<div eID="gen42582" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42583" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">dogs--</hi>Greek, "the dogs"; the impure, filthy (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.11">Re 22:11</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Phil.3.2">Php 3:2</reference>).<div eID="gen42583" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42584" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">maketh--</hi>including also "whosoever practiceth a lie" [W. Kelly]. <div eID="gen42584" type="x-p"/>
entries.4f8e9d094e4a635a6ca700ffe1ac9fc7dbaaf973: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19435"/><div sID="gen42585" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19435"/><hi type="bold">16. mine angel--</hi>for Jesus is Lord of the angels.<div eID="gen42585" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42586" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto you--</hi>ministers and people in the seven representative churches, and, through you, to testify to Christians of all times and places.<div eID="gen42586" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42587" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">root ... offspring of David--</hi>appropriate title here where assuring His Church of "the sure mercies of David," secured to Israel first, and through Israel to the Gentiles. Root of David, as being Jehovah; the offspring of David as man. David's Lord, yet David's son (<reference osisRef="Matt.22.42-Matt.22.45">Mt 22:42-45</reference>).<div eID="gen42587" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42588" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the morning star--</hi>that ushered in the day of grace in the beginning of this dispensation and that shall usher in the everlasting day of glory at its close. <div eID="gen42588" type="x-p"/>
entries.6cbcfc339b86cca902ee4745041bde6334acdc67: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19436"/><div sID="gen42589" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19436"/>17. Reply of the spiritual Church and John to Christ's words (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.7">Re 22:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.12.16">12, 16</reference>).<div eID="gen42589" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42590" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the Spirit--</hi>in the churches and in the prophets.<div eID="gen42590" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42591" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the bride--</hi>not here called "wife," as that title applies to her only when the full number constituting the Church shall have been completed. The invitation, "Come," only holds good while the Church is still but an affianced Bride, and not the actually wedded wife. However, "Come" may rather be the prayer of the Spirit in the Church and in believers in reply to Christ's "I come quickly," crying, Even so, "Come" (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.7">Re 22:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.12">12</reference>); <reference osisRef="Rev.22.20">Re 22:20</reference> confirms this view. The whole question of your salvation hinges on this, that you be able to hear with joy Christ's announcement, "I come," and to reply, "Come" [Bengel]. Come to fully glorify Thy Bride.<div eID="gen42591" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42592" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">let him that heareth--</hi>that is, let him that heareth the Spirit and Bride saying to the Lord Jesus, "Come," join the Bride as a true believer, become part of her, and so say with her to Jesus, "Come." On "heareth" means "obeyeth"; for until one has obeyed the Gospel call, he cannot pray to Jesus "Come"; so "hear" is used, <reference osisRef="Rev.1.3">Re 1:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.10.16">Joh 10:16</reference>. Let him that hears and obeys Jesus' voice (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.16">Re 22:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.1.3">Re 1:3</reference>) join in praying "Come." Compare <reference osisRef="Rev.6.1">Re 6:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.6.10">10</reference>; see on <reference osisRef="Rev.6.1">Re 6:1</reference>. In the other view, which makes "Come" an invitation to sinners, this clause urges those who themselves hear savingly the invitation to address the same to others, as did Andrew and Philip after they themselves had heard and obeyed Jesus' invitation, "Come."<div eID="gen42592" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42593" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">let him that is athirst come--</hi>As the Bride, the Church, prays to Jesus, "Come," so she urges all whosoever thirst for participation in the full manifestation of redemption-glory at His coming to us, to COME in the meantime and drink of the living waters, which are the earnest of "the water of life pure as crystal ... out of the throne of God of the Lamb" (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.1">Re 22:1</reference>) in the regenerated heaven and earth.<div eID="gen42593" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42594" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">And--</hi>so Syriac. But A, B, Vulgate, and Coptic omit "and."<div eID="gen42594" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42595" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">whosoever will--</hi>that is, is willing and desirous. There is a descending climax; Let him that heareth effectually and savingly Christ's voice, pray individually, as the Bride, the Church, does collectively, "Come, Lord Jesus" (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.20">Re 22:20</reference>). Let him who, though not yet having actually heard unto salvation, and so not yet able to join in the prayer, "Lord Jesus, come, "still thirsts for it, come to Christ. Whosoever is even willing, though his desires do not yet amount to positive thirsting, let him take the water of life freely, that is, gratuitously. <div eID="gen42595" type="x-p"/>
entries.9394f62b5d1c94c0795309c8858aa8d1effbb030: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19437"/><div sID="gen42596" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19437"/><hi type="bold">18. For I testify--</hi>None of our manuscripts have this. A, B, Vulgate, and Andreas read, "I" emphatic in the Greek. "I testify."<div eID="gen42596" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42597" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto these things--</hi>A, B, and Andreas read, "unto them."<div eID="gen42597" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42598" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">add ... add--</hi>just retribution in kind. <div eID="gen42598" type="x-p"/>
entries.ced59a4cd74442f4e70f03e35aa74a2a1d37534e: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19438"/><div sID="gen42599" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19438"/><hi type="bold">19. book--</hi>None of our manuscripts read this. A, B, Aleph, Vulgate, Syriac, and Coptic read, "(take away his part, that is, portion) from the tree of life," that is, shall deprive him of participation in the tree of life.<div eID="gen42599" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42600" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and from the things--</hi>so Vulgate. But A, B, Aleph, Syriac, Coptic, and Andreas omit "and"; then "which are written in this book" will refer to "the holy city and the tree of life." As in the beginning of this book (<reference osisRef="Rev.1.3">Re 1:3</reference>) a blessing was promised to the devout, obedient student of it, so now at its close a curse is denounced against those who add to, or take from, it. <div eID="gen42600" type="x-p"/>
entries.9c15312d0c2c86d7d8e4c68135fed422757b41a5: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19439"/><div sID="gen42601" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19439"/><hi type="bold">20. Amen. Even so, come--</hi>The Song of Solomon (<reference osisRef="Song.8.14">So 8:14</reference>) closes with the same yearning prayer for Christ's coming. A, B, and Aleph omit "Even so," Greek, "nai": then translate for Amen, "So be it, come, Lord Jesus"; joining the "Amen," or "So be it," not with Christ's saying (for He calls Himself the "Amen" at the beginning of sentences, rather than puts it as a confirmation at the end), but with John's reply. Christ's "I come," and John's "Come," are almost coincident in time; so truly does the believer reflect the mind of his Lord. <div eID="gen42601" type="x-p"/>
entries.cbdf4074e29b0c1169f78023cbe3ba4639fa9ba4: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19440"/><div sID="gen42602" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19440"/><hi type="bold">21. our--</hi>so Vulgate, Syriac, and Coptic. But A, B, and Aleph omit.<div eID="gen42602" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42603" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Christ--</hi>so B, Vulgate, Syriac, Coptic, and Andreas. But A and Aleph omit.<div eID="gen42603" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42604" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">with you all--</hi>so none of our manuscripts. B has, "with all the saints." A and Vulgate have, "with all." Aleph has, "with the saints." This closing benediction, Paul's mark in his Epistles, was after Paul's death taken up by John. The Old Testament ended with a "curse" in connection with the law; the New Testament ends with a blessing in union with the Lord Jesus.<div eID="gen42604" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42605" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Amen--</hi>so B, Aleph, and Andreas. A and Vulgate Fuldensis omit it.<div eID="gen42605" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42606" type="x-p"/> May the Blessed Lord who has caused all holy Scriptures to be written for our learning, bless this humble effort to make Scripture expound itself, and make it an instrument towards the conversion of sinners and the edification of saints, to the glory of His great name and the hastening of His kingdom! Amen. __________________________________________________________________  <chapter eID="Rev.22"/><div eID="gen42606" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen41184" osisID="Rev" type="book"/>

entries.0cb2d4c193e287861e587e8437d6572675cd5de3: <div eID="gen56832" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen56833" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen56834" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen56834" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen56833" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen56835" type="x-p"/> The river of the water of life, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.1">Rev 22:1</reference>. The tree of life, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.2">Rev 22:2</reference>. There is no curse nor darkness in the city of God, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.3-Rev.22.5">Rev 22:3-5</reference>. The angel assures John of the truth of what he has heard, and states that the time of the fulfillment is at hand, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.6">Rev 22:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.7">Rev 22:7</reference>. He forbids John to worship him, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.8">Rev 22:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.9">Rev 22:9</reference>. Again he states that the time of the fulfillment of the prophecies of this book is at hand, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.10-Rev.22.12">Rev 22:10-12</reference>. Christ is Alpha and Omega, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.13">Rev 22:13</reference>. The blessedness of those who keep his commandments; they enter through the gates into the city, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.14">Rev 22:14</reference>. All the unholy are excluded, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.15">Rev 22:15</reference>. Christ sent his angel to testify of those things in the Churches, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.16">Rev 22:16</reference>. The invitation of the Spirit and the bride, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.17">Rev 22:17</reference>. A curse denounced against those who shall either add to or take away front the prophecies of this book, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.18">Rev 22:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.19">Rev 22:19</reference>. Christ cometh quickly, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.20">Rev 22:20</reference>. The apostolical benediction, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.21">Rev 22:21</reference>. <div eID="gen56835" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56836" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen56836" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56837" type="x-p"/> Pure river of water of life - This is evidently a reference to the garden of paradise, and the river by which it was watered; and there is also a reference to the account, <reference osisRef="Eze.47.7-Eze.47.12">Eze 47:7-12</reference>. Water of life, as we have seen before, generally signifies spring or running water; here it may signify incessant communications of happiness proceeding from God.
entries.b74670fc86b3783c18cb05207c61238674ff369c: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen56837" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56838" type="x-p"/> In the midst of the street of it - That is, of the city which was described in the preceding chapter. <div eID="gen56838" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56839" type="x-p"/> The tree of life - An allusion to <reference osisRef="Gen.2.9">Gen 2:9</reference>. As this tree of life is stated to be in the streets of the city, and on each side of the river, tree must here be an enallage of the singular for the plural number, trees of life, or trees which yielded fruit by which life was preserved. The account in Ezekiel is this: "And by the river, upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade - it shall bring forth new fruit, according to his months - and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine;" <reference osisRef="Eze.47.12">Eze 47:12</reference>. <div eID="gen56839" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56840" type="x-p"/> Twelve manner of fruits - Καρπους δωδεκα· Twelve fruits; that is, fruit twelve times in the year, as is immediately explained, yielded her fruit every month. As this was a great and spacious city, one fountain was not sufficient to provide water for it, therefore a river is mentioned; a great river, by which it was sufficiently watered. Some think that by this tree of life the Gospel is indicated; the twelve fruits are the twelve apostles; and the leaves are Gospel doctrines by which the nations - the Gentiles, are healed of the disease of sin. But this seems to be a fanciful interpretation.
entries.465f5ff3646d18daf53b3981bd975e7392e4bffc: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen56840" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56841" type="x-p"/> No more curse - Instead of καταναθεμα, curse, the best MSS., versions, etc., read καταθεμα cursed person. As there shall be no more sinning against God, so there shall be no more curse of God upon the people; for they shall be all his servants, and serve him. Our first parents came under the curse by sinning against their Maker in paradise; these shall never apostatize, therefore neither they nor the earth shall be cursed.
entries.9472a7770589c6380fde41f90f02fd4e4881c33d: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen56841" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56842" type="x-p"/> See his face - Enjoy what is called the beatific vision; and they shall exhibit the fullest evidence that they belong entirely to him, for his name shall be written on their foreheads.
entries.822ae1c487aa858b7c57a4842f86eacb8aa6d493: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen56842" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56843" type="x-p"/> There shall be no night there - See the 23d (note) and 25th (note) verses of the preceding chapter (<reference osisRef="Rev.21.23">Rev 21:23</reference> and <reference osisRef="Rev.21.25">Rev 21:25</reference>).
entries.b2f7b3ae5b512749c8902ad951d53075ac6fbe38: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen56843" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56844" type="x-p"/> These sayings are faithful and true - See the preceding chapter, <reference osisRef="Rev.21.5">Rev 21:5</reference>. From this verse to the end of the chapter is reckoned the epilogue of this book. <div eID="gen56844" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56845" type="x-p"/> 1. The angel affirms the truth of all that had been spoken, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.6-Rev.22.11">Rev 22:6-11</reference>. <div eID="gen56845" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56846" type="x-p"/> 2. Jesus Christ confirms what has been affirmed, and pledges himself for the fulfillment of all the prophecies contained in it, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.12-Rev.22.17">Rev 22:12-17</reference>. <div eID="gen56846" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56847" type="x-p"/> 3. John cautions his readers against adding or diminishing, and concludes with the apostolical blessing, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.18-Rev.22.21">Rev 22:18-21</reference>. <div eID="gen56847" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56848" type="x-p"/> The things which must shortly be done - There are many sayings in this book which, if taken literally, would intimate that the prophecies delivered in the whole of the Apocalypse were to be fulfilled in a short time after their delivery to John; and this is a strong support for the scheme of Wetstein, and those who maintain that the prophecies of this book all referred to those times in which the apostle lived, and to the disturbances which then took place, not only among the Jews, but in the Roman empire. What they all mean, and when and how they are to be fulfilled, God in heaven alone knows.
entries.4b9bb1abc0d1eeaca5ccd508e282c6634202e077: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen56848" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56849" type="x-p"/> I fell down to worship - I prostrated myself before him as before a superior being, to express my gratitude, and give him thanks for the communications he had made. See on <reference osisRef="Rev.19.10">Rev 19:10</reference> (note).
entries.e7610864495dc7561569ec0729adcfb1c6d9b5ae: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen56849" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56850" type="x-p"/> Seal not the sayings - Do not lay them up for future generations; they concern the present times; they must shortly come to pass, for the time is at hand. See above, <reference osisRef="Rev.22.6">Rev 22:6</reference>. What concerned the Jews was certainly at hand.
entries.39d076d38f85b26eed56ee93cd379e0c639b67d8: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen56850" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56851" type="x-p"/> He that is unjust, let him be unjust still - The time of fulfillment will come so suddenly that there will be but little space for repentance and amendment. What is done must be done instantly; and let him that is holy persevere, and hold fast what he has received.
entries.90deff0f1847101f636f996cfb14ecf04c7808d6: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen56851" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56852" type="x-p"/> Behold, I come quickly - I come to establish nay cause, comfort and support my followers, and punish the wicked.
entries.9ba863572ac5c667af7d3b6143b96e3b9b8aeab5: <hi type="bold">Verse 13</hi> <div eID="gen56852" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56853" type="x-p"/> I am Alpha and Omega - See on <reference osisRef="Rev.1.8">Rev 1:8</reference> (note), <reference osisRef="Rev.1.18">Rev 1:18</reference> (note).
entries.1351384e5a7e4fffe0882b0efb5a45569452f86a: <hi type="bold">Verse 14</hi> <div eID="gen56853" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56854" type="x-p"/> Blessed are they that do his commandments - They are happy who are obedient. <div eID="gen56854" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56855" type="x-p"/> That they may have right to the tree of life - The original is much more expressive, Ἱνα εσται ἡ εξουσια αυτων επι το ξυλον της ζωης· That they may have authority over the tree of life; an authority founded on right, this right founded on obedience to the commandments of God, and that obedience produced by the grace of God working in them. Without grace no obedience; without obedience no authority to the tree of life; without authority no right; without right no enjoyment: God's grace through Christ produces the good, and then rewards it as if all had been our own.
entries.8222710ff3ec2dd42ceea0b1dfc81ed98e7e1397: <hi type="bold">Verse 15</hi> <div eID="gen56855" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56856" type="x-p"/> Without are dogs - All those who are uncircumcised in heart. The Jews call all the uncircumcised dogs. "Who is a dog? Ans. He who is not circumcised." Pirkey Elieser, chap. 29. <div eID="gen56856" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56857" type="x-p"/> And sorcerers - See the note on <reference osisRef="Rev.21.8">Rev 21:8</reference>.
entries.7a505f4dfc131c4dd4a3f315decc0ee88f40f52d: <hi type="bold">Verse 16</hi> <div eID="gen56857" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56858" type="x-p"/> I Jesus - The Maker, the Redeemer, and Judge of all men. <div eID="gen56858" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56859" type="x-p"/> Have sent mine angel - An especial messenger from heaven. <div eID="gen56859" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56860" type="x-p"/> I am the root and the offspring of David - Christ is the root of David as to his Divine nature; for from that all the human race sprang, for he is the Creator of all things, and without him was nothing made which is made. And he is the offspring of David as to his human nature; for that he took of the stock of David, becoming thereby heir to the Jewish throne, and the only heir which then existed; and it is remarkable that the whole regal family terminated in Christ: and as He liveth for ever, he is the alone true David and everlasting King. <div eID="gen56860" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56861" type="x-p"/> The bright and morning star - I am splendor and glory to my kingdom; as the morning star ushers in the sun, so shall I usher in the unclouded and eternal glories of the everlasting kingdom.
entries.97d6fdcf1cdf55dd557252bfde4575f6d4e87097: <hi type="bold">Verse 17</hi> <div eID="gen56861" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56862" type="x-p"/> The Spirit and the bride - All the prophets and all the apostles; the Church of God under the Old Testament, and the Church of Christ under the New. <div eID="gen56862" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56863" type="x-p"/> Say, Come - Invite men to Jesus, that by him they may be saved and prepared for this kingdom. <div eID="gen56863" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56864" type="x-p"/> Let him that heareth - Let all who are privileged with reading and hearing the word of God, join in the general invitation to sinners. <div eID="gen56864" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56865" type="x-p"/> Him that is athirst - He who feels his need of salvation, and is longing to drink of the living fountain. <div eID="gen56865" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56866" type="x-p"/> And whosoever will - No soul is excluded: Jesus died for every man; every man may be saved; therefore let him who wills, who wishes for salvation, come and take the water of life freely - without money or price!
entries.74218f1442d81723cc3ced5db3f0212f78af353e: <hi type="bold">Verse 18</hi> <div eID="gen56866" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56867" type="x-p"/> If any man shall add - Shall give any other meaning to these prophecies, or any other application of them than God intends, he, though not originally intended, shall have the plagues threatened in this book for his portion.
entries.6c6aa170df09985ea8b2591c91cdc6ab939ca199: <hi type="bold">Verse 19</hi> <div eID="gen56867" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56868" type="x-p"/> If any man shall take away - If any man shall lessen this meaning, curtail the sense, explain away the spirit and design, of these prophecies, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, etc. Thus Jesus Christ warns all those who consider this book to beware of indulging their own conjectures concerning it. I confess that this warning has its own powerful influence upon my mind, and has prevented me from indulging my own conjectures concerning its meaning, or of adopting the conjectures of others. These visions and threatenings are too delicate and awful a subject to trifle with, or even to treat in the most solemn manner, where the meaning is obscure. I must leave these things to time and event, the surest interpreters. No jot or tittle of Christ's word shall fall to the ground; all shall have its fulfillment in due time. <div eID="gen56868" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56869" type="x-p"/> This is termed a revelation, but it is a revelation of symbols; an exhibition of enigmas, to which no particular solution is given, and to which God alone can give the solution.
entries.7acffa1d8512919d717a6f9200925f4af5cb95e1: <hi type="bold">Verse 20</hi> <div eID="gen56869" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56870" type="x-p"/> Surely I come quickly - This may be truly said to every person in every age; Jesus the Judge is at the door! <div eID="gen56870" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56871" type="x-p"/> Even so, come, Lord Jesus - The wish and desire of the suffering Church, and of all the followers of God, who are longing for the coming of his kingdom.
entries.d86ac9f48719079ce2c7911b349333aeb081b578: <hi type="bold">Verse 21</hi> <div eID="gen56871" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56872" type="x-p"/> The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ - May the favor and powerful influence of Jesus Christ be with you all; you of the seven Churches, and the whole Church of Christ in every part of the earth, and through all the periods of time. <div eID="gen56872" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56873" type="x-p"/> Instead of παντων ὑμων, you all, the most excellent MSS. and versions have παντων των ἁγιων, all the saints. This reading Griesbach has received into the text as indisputably genuine. <div eID="gen56873" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56874" type="x-p"/> Amen - So be it! and so shall it be for ever and ever. The opinion of Dr. Priestley, concerning the authenticity of this book, and the manner in which it is written, should not be withheld from either the learned or pious reader. "I think it impossible for any intelligent and candid person to peruse this book without being struck in the most forcible manner with the peculiar dignity and sublimity of its composition, superior to that of any other writing whatever; so as to be convinced that, considering the age in which it appeared, none but a person divinely inspired could have written it. These prophecies are also written in such a manner as to satisfy us that the events announced to us were really foreseen, being described in such a manner as no person writing without that knowledge could have done. This requires such a mixture of clearness and obscurity as has never yet been imitated by any forgers of prophecy whatever. Forgeries, written of course after the events, have always been too plain. It is only in the Scriptures, and especially in the book of Daniel, and this of the Revelation, that we find this happy mixture of clearness and obscurity in the accounts of future events." - Notes on Revelation. <div eID="gen56874" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56875" type="x-p"/> The Subscriptions to this book are both few and unimportant: - <div eID="gen56875" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56876" type="x-p"/> The Codex Alexandrinus has simply - The Revelation of John. <div eID="gen56876" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56877" type="x-p"/> The Syriac doubles the Amen. <div eID="gen56877" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56878" type="x-p"/> The Ethiopic. - Here is ended the vision of John, the Apocalypse; Amen: this is, as one might say, the vision which he saw in his life; and it was written by the blessed John, the evangelist of God. <div eID="gen56878" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56879" type="x-p"/> Vulgate and Coptic nothing. <div eID="gen56879" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56880" type="x-p"/> Ancient Arabic. - By the assistance of our Lord Jesus Christ, the vision of John, the apostle and evangelist, the beloved of the Lord, is finished: this is the Apocalypse which the Lord revealed to him for the service of men. To Him be glory for ever and ever. <div eID="gen56880" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56881" type="x-p"/> Having now brought my short notes on this very obscure book to a conclusion, it may be expected that, although I do not adopt any of the theories which have been delivered concerning it, yet I should give the most plausible scheme of the ancients or moderns which has come to my knowledge. This I would gladly do if I had any scheme to which I could give a decided preference. However, as I have given in the preface the scheme of Professor Wetstein, it is right that I should, at the conclusion, give the scheme of Mr. Lowman, which is nearly the same with that of Bishop Newton, and which, as far as I can learn, is considered by the most rational divines as being the most consistent and probable. <div eID="gen56881" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56882" type="x-p"/> The scheme of the learned and pious Bengel may be found in the late Rev. John Wesley's notes on this book; that of Mr. Lowman, which now follows, may he found at the end of Dr. Dodd's notes. <div eID="gen56882" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56883" type="x-p"/> Among other objections to this and all such schemes, I have this, which to me appears of vital consequence; its dates are too late. I think the book was written before the destruction of Jerusalem, and not in 95 or 96, the date which I follow in the margin; which date I give, not as my own opinion, but the opinion of others.  <chapter eID="Rev.22"/> <div eID="gen56883" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen55581" osisID="Rev" type="book"/>

entries.667ed105c154299f9fa21e005949b601f84bc005:
Verse 1. And he showed me a pure river of water of life. In the New Jerusalem; the happy abode of the redeemed. The phrase "water of life," means living or running water, like a spring or fountain, as contrasted with a stagnant pool. Jn 4:14. The allusion here is doubtless to the first Eden, where a river watered the garden, (Gen 2:10, seq.,) and as this is a description of Eden recovered, or Paradise regained, it was natural to introduce a river of water also, yet in such a way as to accord with the general description of that future abode of the redeemed. It does not spring up, therefore, from the ground, but flows from the throne of God and the Lamb. Perhaps, also, the writer had in his eye the description in Eze 47:1-12, where a stream issues from under the temple, and is parted in different directions.

Clear as crystal. Rev 4:6.

Proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb. Flowing from the foot of the throne. Compare Rev 4:6. This idea is strictly in accordance with Oriental imagery. In the East, fountains and running streams constituted an essential part of the image of enjoyment and prosperity, (Isa 35:6,) and such fountains were common in the courts of Oriental houses. Here, the river is an emblem of peace, happiness, plenty; and the essential thought in its flowing from the throne is, that all the happiness of heaven proceeds from God.
entries.6dc7f4346e1ef607f421ec559fa92102249cdfe4:
Verse 2. In the midst of the street of it. Professor Stuart renders this, "between the street thereof and the river;" and says that "the writer conceives of the river as running through the whole city; then of streets parallel to it on either side; and then, on the banks of the river, between the water and the street, the whole stream is lined on either side with two rows of the tree of life." The more common interpretation, however, is doubtless admissible, and would give a more beautiful image; that in the street, or streets of the city, as well as on the banks of the river, the tree of life was planted. It abounded everywhere. The city had not only a river passing through it, but it was pervaded by streets, and all those streets were lined and shaded with this tree. The idea in the mind of the writer is that of Eden or Paradise; but it is not the Eden of the book of Genesis, or the Oriental or Persian Paradise: it is a picture where all is combined that in the view of the writer would constitute beauty, or contribute to happiness.

And on either side of the river. As well as in all the streets. The writer undoubtedly conceives of a single river running through the city--probably as meandering along--and that river lined on both sides with the tree of life. This gives great beauty to the imagery.

Was there the tree of life. Not a single tree, but it abounded everywhere--on the banks of the river, and in all the streets. It was the common tree in this blessed Paradise--of which all might partake, and which was everywhere the emblem of immortality. In this respect, this new Paradise stands in strong contrast with that in which Adam was placed at his creation, where there seems to have been a single tree that was designated as the tree of life, Gen 3:22-23. In the future state of the blessed, that tree will abound, and all may freely partake of it; the emblem--the pledge of immortal life--will be constantly before the eyes, whatever part of the future abode may be traversed, and the inhabitants of that blessed world may constantly partake of it.

Which bare twelve manner of fruits. "Producing twelve fruit-harvests; not (as our version) twelve manner of fruits."--Professor Stuart. The idea is not that there are twelve kinds of fruit on the same tree, for that is not implied in the language used by John. The literal rendering is, "producing twelve fruits"--ποιουνκαρπουςδωδεκα. The word "manner" has been introduced by the translators without authority. The idea is, that the tree bore every month in the year, so that there were twelve fruit-harvests. It was not like a tree that bears but once a year, or in one season only, but it constantly bore fruit--it bore every month. The idea is that of abundance, not variety. The supply never fails; the tree is never barren. As there is but a single class of trees referred to, it might have been supposed, perhaps, that, according to the common method in which fruit is produced, there would be sometimes plenty and sometimes want; but the writer says that, though there is but one kind, yet the supply is ample. The tree is everywhere; it is constantly producing fruit.

And yielded her fruit every month. The word "and" is also supplied by the translators, and introduces an idea which is not in the original, as if there was not only a sucession of harvests, which is in the text, but that each one differed from the former, which is not in the text. The proper translation is, "producing twelve fruits, yielding or rendering its fruit in each month." Thus there is indeed a succession of fruit-crops, but it is the same kind of fruit. We are not to infer, however, that there will not be variety in the occupations and the joys of the heavenly state, for there can be no doubt that there will be ample diversity in the employments, and in the sources of happiness, in heaven; but the single thought expressed here is, that the means of life will be abundant: the trees of life will be everywhere, and they will be constantly yielding fruit.

And the leaves of the tree. Not only the fruit will contribute to give life, but even the leaves will be salutary. Everything about it will contribute to sustain life.

Were for the healing. That is, they contribute to impart life and health to those who had been diseased. We are not to suppose that there will be sickness, and a healing process in heaven, for that idea is expressly excluded in Rev 21:4; but the meaning is, that the life and health of that blessed world will have been imparted by partaking of that tree, and the writer says that, in fact, it was owing to it that they who dwell there had been healed of their spiritual maladies, and had been made to live for ever.

Of the nations. Of all the nations assembled there, Rev 21:24. There is a close resemblance between the language here used by John and that used by Ezekiel, (Eze 47:12,) and it is not improbable that both these writers refer to the same thing. Compare also, in the Apocrypha, 2 Esdras ii. 12; viii. 52-54.

(a) "In the midst" Eze 47:1,12 (b) "street" Rev 21:21 (c) "tree of life" Rev 2:7
entries.3b03cc4dae30d658f24de1b345d5ce8937cb8483:
Verse 3. And there shall be no more curse. This is doubtless designed to be in strong contrast with our present abode; and it is affirmed that what now properly comes under the name of a curse, or whatever is part of the curse pronounced on man by the fall, will be there unknown. The earth will be no more cursed, and will produce no more thorns and thistles; man will be no more compelled to earn his bread by the sweat of his brow; woman will be no more doomed to bear the sufferings which she does now; and the abodes of the blessed will be no more cursed by sickness, sorrow, tears, and death.

But the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it. God will reign there for ever; the principles of purity and love which the Lamb of God came to establish will pervade that blessed abode to all eternity.

And his servants shall serve him. All his servants that are there; that is, all the inhabitants of that blessed world. For the meaning of this passage, Rev 7:15.

(d) "no more curse" Zech 14:11 (e) "throne of God" Eze 48:35 (f) "servants" Rev 7:15

Verse 4. And they shall see his face. Mt 18:10. They would be constantly in his presence, and be permitted continually to behold his glory.

And his name shall be in their foreheads. They shall be designated as his. Rev 3:12; Rev 7:3; Rev 13:16.

(g) "And they shall" Mt 5:8, Jn 12:26, 17:24, 1Cor 13:12, 1Jn 3:2 (h) "his name" Rev 3:12

Verse 5. And there shall be no night there. Rev 21:25.

And they need no candle. No lamp; no artificial light, as in a world where there is night and darkness.

Neither light of the sun; for the Lord God, etc. Rev 21:23.

And they shall reign for ever and ever. That is, with God; they shall be as kings. Rev 5:10; Rev 20:6. Compare Rom 8:16; 2Ti 1:11 2Ti 1:12.
